I have a theory that what everyone is drinking at a show can tell you a lot about the mood of a crowd, and based on the stacks of Hard Solo and Walker cans strewn on the streets outside Dom Dolla’s biggest ever show, 60,000 people are in for an intense, sticky night. And a significant one. That 60,000 people… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.
item.dc:creator: Sian Cain

item.title: ‘Everyone can relate to pain and struggle. So I’m sharing mine’: Michael Kiwanuka on life after his devastating stroke
item.description: The Mercury prize winner hasn’t been able to go home since falling ill last summer. In his only interview, he opens up about the ‘poignancy’ of finally releasing the new album his stroke shelved At the end of July 2025, Michael Kiwanuka was back home in Southampton after a series of European gigs. His 2024 album Small Changes had been critically acclaimed and was kept off the UK No 1 slot only by Kendrick Lamar’s GNX. His fifth record, Fudge, was due that autumn. All was going perfectly for the virtuoso singer-songwriter, whose eccentric, genre-busting mix of psychedelic rock, prog soul… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.
item.dc:creator: Jason Okundaye

item.title: El cisma con una secta católica rebelde ensombrece la visita del papa León a Francia
item.description: La excomunión de la Fraternidad Sacerdotal San Pío X plantea al papa León XIV una situación delicada en Francia, donde esta comunidad integrista está muy arraigada, con un centenar de lugares de culto y una red de colegios no concertados. Por su parte, los miembros de la Fraternidad esperan que se adopten posturas firmes sobre la eutanasia y el aborto. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Ai Weiwei unveils his epic new Australian work: ‘90% of art is just garbage. Real art questions the existing order’
item.description: From his farm in Portugal, the acclaimed artist speaks about war, peace, the state of the world – and his 40 metre sculpture Mushrooms, on Sydney Harbour “It’s like a film set. Like it’s not real,” the bemused Uber driver says as we pass through a succession of silent rural villages washed with milky sunlight. He’s right: signs of human life are weirdly absent during our windy journey through the Alentejo. I’m making my way to Ai Weiwei’s secluded farm, nestled deep in the Portuguese countryside, where arguably the world’s best known living artist has quietly lived for the last six years… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.

item.description: Melania Trump and China’s first lady Peng Liyuan toured Chinese artworks and a room shaped by Asian design at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art in Washington on Thursday, as their husbands held talks at the White House. The museum’s director, Chase Robinson, said the two women spent about 45 minutes there and were “full of questions”.
